# Researching and ingesting wiki evidence

Choose the mode explicitly from the request. An unspecified request to use this
role is not permission to process the whole backlog; clarify the intended task.
Treat `` as the request when the host has not substituted it.

- **Discover sources on a topic:** read [discovery](references/discover.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), and
  [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md). Research perspectives
  return candidates without writing. Use the capture route only within the
  requested scope; a request for candidates alone remains read-only.
- **Capture named URLs or saved web pages:** read [named capture](references/capture.md)
  and [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md). Skip broad topic research;
  preserve deduplication, declines and capture checks.
- **Capture a named format or service:** read its complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or
  [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md). These routes include prerequisite
  checks; missing converters or authentication never justify fabricated evidence.
- **Ingest named existing clippings:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md),
  [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), and
  [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md). Use the exact source set;
  do not rediscover it or silently expand to the global backlog.
- **Process new or un-ingested clippings without a filename:** read
  [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join backlog contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Determine eligibility before writing. Preserve already summarized sources and
  reject restricted evidence as support. If nothing eligible is pending, report
  that without opening an operation, logging, committing or refreshing indexes.

Capture-only requests create evidence, never derived source or concept pages.
Ingestion needs authorization for that source set; an explicitly requested full
research-and-ingest flow already provides it. Only capture tools write raw
artifacts, and agents never edit their bodies. Read
[evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before assessing fidelity,
quoting or synthesizing; preserve restrictions and platform-specific sections.

Before the first authorized mutation, read
[operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Finish the
scoped validation, log, commit, sync and remote verification unless publication
is held. Reuse an enclosing operation when it owns the work; preserve other
writers' edits. For concept reuse and relationship changes read
[efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).

5	# Clipping a GitHub repository into the wiki
6	
7	A GitHub repository is not one document — it is dozens, hundreds, or (for a
8	real enterprise monorepo) many thousands of files, each independently
9	citable. The HTML clipper (`clip.mjs` → Defuddle) reads a repo's
10	HTML landing page and gets a thin, mostly-chrome extraction; `clip-docx`/
11	`clip-pdf` don't apply at all. This reference covers the repo path, and it is
12	deliberately **not** "dump the whole tree into one file" — nor, for a large
13	repo, "dump the whole tree as one clipping per file" either. `clip-gh.mjs`
14	clones the repo to a **temp directory** (cleaned up afterward; the clone
15	itself never touches the vault), walks its real files, excludes
16	dependency/build/binary/oversized noise, and then picks one of two output
17	shapes depending on size:
18	
19	- **Per-file mode** (repo has ≤300 includable files, the default cap): one
20	  clipping per included file under `raw/clippings/gh/<owner>/<repo>/`, plus
21	  one `_repo-overview.md` manifest. Multiple small, citable clippings beat
22	  one giant unquotable blob — the same reasoning behind every other `clip-*`
23	  script's per-item output.
24	- **Digest mode** (repo is over the cap): a manifest + a **bounded** number
25	  of per-module *listing* documents (never one per file) + a small set of
26	  full-content clips for universally valuable "anchor" files. See its own
27	  section below — this is the mode a large repo actually needs, and the one
28	  most likely to matter for an internal platform/monorepo clip.
29	
30	## How it works
31	
32	`clip-gh.mjs` shells out to the **`gh` CLI** (`gh repo clone owner/repo <tmp>
33	-- --depth 1`), so cloning transparently uses the user's existing `gh auth`
34	session — private repos the user can already see on the command line work
35	with no extra config. It never runs a bare `git clone`, and it never writes
36	into the temp clone's own `.git` history.
37	
38	**"Don't clip the whole repo contents" is enforced by three curated
39	exclusion rules, not full `.gitignore` parsing:**
40	- **Directories**, matched by name at any depth: `.git`, `node_modules`,
41	  `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `.venv`/`venv`, `__pycache__`, `.next`,
42	  `.nuxt`, `coverage`, `.terraform`, `bower_components`. (`.github/` is
43	  deliberately **not** excluded — CI workflow YAML is real, clippable
44	  content; only the specific named directories above are.)
45	- **Extensions**, binary/media/archive/compiled: images, fonts, archives,
46	  executables/object files, audio/video, PDFs, databases.
47	- **Exact basenames**, generated lockfiles: `package-lock.json`,
48	  `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `Gemfile.lock`,
49	  `composer.lock`, `go.sum`.
50	- **Size ceiling**: 256 KB per file, regardless of extension.
51	
52	### Per-file mode (small repos)
53	
54	Each **included** file becomes one clipping: a `.md`/`.mdx` file is stored
55	as-is (never re-fenced — fencing a Markdown file would nest its own headings
56	and code fences inside an outer fence and break both); every other file is
57	wrapped in a language-hinted fenced code block (```javascript, ```python,
58	etc. — a small lookup table, not exhaustive; falls back to a bare fence with
59	no hint for anything unrecognized) so it reads as quotable source. The
60	citation is the file's real GitHub blob URL at the exact commit clipped
61	(`.../blob/<sha-or-ref>/<path>`), not the repo root — so a later reader lands
62	on the exact file and line range, not a generic landing page. A file whose
63	extracted content is under ~20 words (a stub, a near-empty config) is skipped
64	as **thin** — lower than the ~100-word floor other clippers use, since a real
65	5-line script or config is still worth a clipping even though a 5-line HTML
66	snippet usually isn't.
67	
68	The **`_repo-overview.md`** manifest is the one clipping that represents the
69	repo itself rather than a file in it: it cites the repo's tree URL (not a
70	blob), and lists the description, primary language, ref clipped, and the
71	full included/excluded file lists. It is the natural entry point
72	researcher ingestion reaches for first when summarizing a freshly-clipped repo.
73	
74	### Digest mode (large repos — output bounded, not 1:1 with file count)
75	
76	A large repository can flood the vault graph if every file becomes a separate
77	clipping before ingestion. Digest mode keeps the capture bounded:
78	
79	- **`_repo-overview.md` (digest manifest)** — description, primary language,
80	  ref, and two BOUNDED tables: a **composition** breakdown (extension →
81	  count — bounded by the number of distinct extensions, not files) and a
82	  **modules** breakdown (module name → file count for every module group,
83	  bounded by the group cap below). Never a per-file bullet list — that
84	  would itself scale 1:1 with file count, the exact thing digest mode
85	  exists to avoid.
86	- **One *listing* document per module group** — a table of file path, size,
87	  and language hint, **never file content**. Groups are computed by
88	  recursively splitting the repo's real directory structure only where a
89	  directory has too many files to summarize in one listing (see
90	  `groupIntoModules` in `clip-gh.mjs` for the exact algorithm), capped at
91	  150 groups by default (`--max-groups=N` to change it) with each group
92	  capped at 150 files before it is split further. A repo with 10 files and
93	  one with 10,000 both produce a small, bounded number of listings — the
94	  big repo's groups are just bigger, up to the cap, never more numerous
95	  without limit. Verify that the sum of every listing's file count equals the
96	  total included count.
97	- **A small set of full-content "anchor" clips** — README (and common
98	  variants/monorepo-package READMEs), LICENSE, CHANGELOG, and top-level
99	  project manifests (`package.json`, `sfdx-project.json`, `pom.xml`,
100	  `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`, etc.), matched by basename only and capped at 15 —
101	  never a heuristic "biggest file" or "most complex" guess, which would have
102	  no principled basis for "important."
103	
104	**Digest mode does NOT try to auto-generate "key modules" or "notable
105	pattern" prose.** That is a genuine summarization/judgment task — reading
106	real code and deciding what is actually architecturally interesting — and
107	belongs in `wiki/sources/` (or `wiki/concepts/`) as a normal, human/agent-
108	curated researcher ingestion-style synthesis citing the digest's manifest and
109	listings as evidence, not something a deterministic extraction script should
110	guess at. After a digest lands, read the manifest's module table plus a
111	representative sample of the largest/most distinctive modules (the listings
112	tell you what exists and roughly how large each module is), then, only when ingestion is authorized, write a
113	**small, bounded** number of `wiki/sources/` pages — a handful, not one per
114	module — covering genuinely notable modules, architectural patterns, or
115	approaches. Conservative: most modules in most repos do not warrant their
116	own write-up; a handful of the most interesting ones do.
117	
118	**Dedup is per-repo, content-hash-based, not URL-based like other
119	`clip-*` scripts**, in both modes. Because a repo clip produces many files,
120	not one, `clip-gh.mjs` reads the `source-hash` already recorded in every
121	existing clipping under that repo's own output directory and skips writing
122	any file whose extracted content hashes the same as before — so re-running
123	against an unchanged repo (or one where most content didn't change) reports
124	things as `unchanged` rather than rewriting them. There is no separate
125	`--decline` re-clip guard keyed on file-within-repo; declines are recorded
126	and checked at the whole-repo level (`github.com/<owner>/<repo>`), same
127	shape as every other source type's decline key.
128	
129	**Digest mode re-clips prune stale listings automatically.** Module
130	grouping is recomputed fresh on every run (see `groupIntoModules`'s own
131	comment for why groups are bounded, not 1:1 with file count) — so a re-clip
132	of a repo that has grown, shrunk, or reorganized enough to cross a
133	splitting threshold can produce different group boundaries than the prior
134	run. Rather than leaving the old run's now-meaningless listings sitting in
135	`raw/` forever (a slow-motion version of exactly the clutter problem digest
136	mode exists to avoid), `clip-gh.mjs` compares this run's expected filenames
137	(manifest + every current listing + every current non-thin anchor) against
138	what is actually in the output directory and deletes anything unexpected,
139	reporting it as `pruned`. After a grouping change, inspect the pruned paths and
140	verify that the module table still accounts for the full included total.
141	This only applies to digest-mode output (listings/manifest/anchors); a
142	per-file-mode clipping for a source file renamed or deleted upstream is
143	**not** currently pruned — that remains a known gap.
144	
145	**Filenames Obsidian can see.** A repo file whose path starts with a dot
146	(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.gitignore`) is clipped as `dot-github-workflows-ci.yml.md`,
147	not `.github-workflows-ci.yml.md`: Obsidian does not index a dot-prefixed file, and the
148	graph walk skips it, so such a clipping can neither be cited nor reach the ingest
149	backlog. A clipping written under the old name is adopted on the next re-clip — renamed
150	to the new name, content untouched — so digest mode's prune cannot delete it and a
151	changed file is updated in place rather than copied. The run reports it as `renamed`.
152	Citations of the old name are repointed by
153	`scripts/rename-unsafe-clippings.mjs` (see [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md)).
154	
155	**No doubled extension.** A repo file is clipped as `README.md`, not `README.md.md`, and a source file
156	keeps its own extension (`src/a.js` is `src-a.js.md`). A doubled file that already exists for a path is kept
157	and updated in place on a re-clip, never copied beside a new one, so no citation breaks;
158	`scripts/rename-doubled-extension-clippings.mjs` renames it together with its citations. If two paths
159	in one run would share a name (`LICENSE` and `LICENSE.md`), the second keeps the doubled form so neither is lost.
160	
161	## Steps
162	
163	1. **Preflight** (once, or whenever a clip fails unexpectedly):
164	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-gh.mjs" --doctor` — reports whether the `gh` CLI
165	   is installed and authenticated.
166	2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for GitHub repos):
167	   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-gh.mjs" <owner/repo | github-url> --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
168	   - Accepts a bare `owner/repo`, a full `https://github.com/owner/repo` URL
169	     (`.git` suffix optional), or a `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` remote —
170	     all resolve to the same identity.
171	   - `--ref=<branch-or-tag>` clips a specific branch/tag instead of the
172	     repo's default branch.
173	   - `--max-files=N` raises the default 300-includable-file per-file-mode
174	     cap. Above the cap, digest mode kicks in automatically (see above) —
175	     nothing is refused silently, and nothing floods the vault with
176	     thousands of files either.
177	   - `--max-groups=N` raises the default 150-module-listing cap in digest
178	     mode, if a repo's real structure warrants more (or fewer) groups than
179	     the default gives it.
180	   - `--force-full` bypasses digest mode and forces the old exhaustive
181	     per-file behavior on a large repo — combine with a `--max-files` raised
182	     past the repo's real file count, since the size cap still applies.
183	     Only reach for this if per-file fidelity on every single file is
184	     genuinely needed; it reintroduces the exact scaling problem digest
185	     mode exists to avoid.
186	   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the
187	     topic string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in
188	     the run, so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together.
189	     **Topic is recorded going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**,
190	     so a clip made without it is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently.
191	     Omit it only when there is no research run behind the clip; never
192	     invent one.
193	   - A `too-many-files` result (only reachable with `--force-full`) means
194	     the cap was hit — re-run with a higher `--max-files` per the message,
195	     or drop `--force-full` to get a digest instead; nothing was written.
196	   - A `failed` result means `gh repo clone` itself errored (bad repo name,
197	     no access, network) — report it for manual handling; do not invent files.
198	3. **Verify** the clippings landed: `ls raw/clippings/gh/<owner>/<repo>/` and
199	   spot-read a few files plus `_repo-overview.md` — confirm the language
200	   fencing and blob-URL citations look right for a couple of samples (per-file
201	   mode), or that the composition/module tables and a listing or two look
202	   sensible (digest mode).
203	4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping batch —
204	   summarize into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Start from
205	   `_repo-overview.md` for the repo-level summary, then pull in individual
206	   files (per-file mode) or a curated set of key-module write-ups informed
207	   by the listings (digest mode) as evidence for specific claims. Ingest only when authorized for this scope; reuse explicit authorization
208	   already supplied in the session.
209	
210	## Guardrails
211	
212	- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped content is
213	  immutable source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state,
214	  tooling-only.
215	- `clip-gh.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for GitHub repos — the model
216	  never writes a clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and
217	  hashing), and never leaves the temporary clone behind (cleaned up in a
218	  `finally`, success or failure).
219	- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful clip of the wrong branch or an outdated
220	  fork is still wrong — confirm the `owner/repo` (and `--ref`, if given) is
221	  the one actually meant before citing it.
222	- **A digest's "key modules" write-ups are synthesis, not evidence** — they
223	  belong in `wiki/sources/` (or `wiki/concepts/`) with `ai-generated: true`
224	  and `sources:` citing the digest's manifest/listings, exactly like any
225	  other ingest summary; never written into `raw/` as if they were
226	  verbatim source content.
227	
228	
229	## Completion
230	
231	For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
232	its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
233	remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
234	use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
235	Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
236	that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
237	create no derived source or concept pages.
238	Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
239	discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.

(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.gitignore`) is clipped as `dot-github-workflows-ci.yml.md`,
not `.github-workflows-ci.yml.md`: Obsidian does not index a dot-prefixed file, and the
graph walk skips it, so such a clipping can neither be cited nor reach the ingest
backlog. A clipping written under the old name is adopted on the next re-clip — renamed
to the new name, content untouched — so digest mode's prune cannot delete it and a
changed file is updated in place rather than copied. The run reports it as `renamed`.
Citations of the old name are repointed by
`scripts/rename-unsafe-clippings.mjs` (see [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md)).

**No doubled extension.** A repo file is clipped as `README.md`, not `README.md.md`, and a source file
keeps its own extension (`src/a.js` is `src-a.js.md`). A doubled file that already exists for a path is kept
and updated in place on a re-clip, never copied beside a new one, so no citation breaks;
`scripts/rename-doubled-extension-clippings.mjs` renames it together with its citations. If two paths
in one run would share a name (`LICENSE` and `LICENSE.md`), the second keeps the doubled form so neither is lost.

## Steps

1. **Preflight** (once, or whenever a clip fails unexpectedly):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-gh.mjs" --doctor` — reports whether the `gh` CLI
   is installed and authenticated.
2. **Clip** (this is the only writer to `raw/` for GitHub repos):
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-gh.mjs" <owner/repo | github-url> --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>"`
   - Accepts a bare `owner/repo`, a full `https://github.com/owner/repo` URL
     (`.git` suffix optional), or a `git@github.com:owner/repo.git` remote —
     all resolve to the same identity.
   - `--ref=<branch-or-tag>` clips a specific branch/tag instead of the
     repo's default branch.
   - `--max-files=N` raises the default 300-includable-file per-file-mode
     cap. Above the cap, digest mode kicks in automatically (see above) —
     nothing is refused silently, and nothing floods the vault with
     thousands of files either.
   - `--max-groups=N` raises the default 150-module-listing cap in digest
     mode, if a repo's real structure warrants more (or fewer) groups than
     the default gives it.
   - `--force-full` bypasses digest mode and forces the old exhaustive
     per-file behavior on a large repo — combine with a `--max-files` raised
     past the repo's real file count, since the size cap still applies.
     Only reach for this if per-file fidelity on every single file is
     genuinely needed; it reintroduces the exact scaling problem digest
     mode exists to avoid.
   - **`--topic` whenever this clip belongs to a research run** — pass the
     topic string researcher discovery was given, identical across every clip in
     the run, so maintainer triage can group the run's leftovers together.
     **Topic is recorded going forward only and no tool can retro-fit it**,
     so a clip made without it is an *Unattributed* triage row permanently.
     Omit it only when there is no research run behind the clip; never
     invent one.
   - A `too-many-files` result (only reachable with `--force-full`) means
     the cap was hit — re-run with a higher `--max-files` per the message,
     or drop `--force-full` to get a digest instead; nothing was written.
   - A `failed` result means `gh repo clone` itself errored (bad repo name,
     no access, network) — report it for manual handling; do not invent files.
3. **Verify** the clippings landed: `ls raw/clippings/gh/<owner>/<repo>/` and
   spot-read a few files plus `_repo-overview.md` — confirm the language
   fencing and blob-URL citations look right for a couple of samples (per-file
   mode), or that the composition/module tables and a listing or two look
   sensible (digest mode).
4. **Only when ingestion is authorized, follow [ingestion](ingest.md)** for this exact clipping batch —
   summarize into `wiki/sources/`, cross-reference, index, log. Start from
   `_repo-overview.md` for the repo-level summary, then pull in individual
   files (per-file mode) or a curated set of key-module write-ups informed
   by the listings (digest mode) as evidence for specific claims. Ingest only when authorized for this scope; reuse explicit authorization
   already supplied in the session.

## Guardrails

- **Never edit the body of anything under `raw/`** — clipped content is
  immutable source-of-truth (guardrail #1). Frontmatter is pipeline state,
  tooling-only.
- `clip-gh.mjs` is the **sole writer** to `raw/` for GitHub repos — the model
  never writes a clipping by hand (that would bypass dedup, decline, and
  hashing), and never leaves the temporary clone behind (cleaned up in a
  `finally`, success or failure).
- **Fidelity, not truth**: a faithful clip of the wrong branch or an outdated
  fork is still wrong — confirm the `owner/repo` (and `--ref`, if given) is
  the one actually meant before citing it.
- **A digest's "key modules" write-ups are synthesis, not evidence** — they
  belong in `wiki/sources/` (or `wiki/concepts/`) with `ai-generated: true`
  and `sources:` citing the digest's manifest/listings, exactly like any
  other ingest summary; never written into `raw/` as if they were
  verbatim source content.


## Completion

For a standalone clip, open an operation before the clipping helper writes, verify
its returned paths and extraction diagnostics, log once, commit, push and verify
remote publication through the shared operations contract. During discovery,
use the enclosing operation and report the results to its owner for completion.
Pass `--since <saved-token>` to the clipping helper so every written path enters
that operation's ledger. Capture-only requests end after this completion and
create no derived source or concept pages.
Capturing evidence does not by itself authorize ingestion; reuse explicit
discover-and-ingest authorization when it is already present.

# Vault access and host commands

Resolve the plugin root from the installed `SKILL.md` location, not the current
working directory: its containing skill folder's `../../` is the plugin root.
From a file in a skill's `references/` folder, use `../../../` instead.
Resolve and quote absolute helper paths before running commands. Treat
`$ARGUMENTS` as the user's request when the host has not substituted it. A linked
skill or reference can be read directly when the host has no skill loader; shared
policy does not require loading the maintenance-role entry point.
Resolve `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT` (default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; with `WIKI_MASTER_REQUIRE_VAULT=1` set and no vault named, a script stops with exit 2 instead of using the default) and verify the expected
vault layout. Read local `AGENTS.md` and schema before edits. A known root and
filesystem access are sufficient for the supported operations below; do not ask
the user to restart Obsidian as a prerequisite for all work.

## Layout and read scope

`raw/clippings/` holds captured evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`
holds maintained pages; `moc/` holds navigational maps; `log/` holds one file per
operation. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it. Reads do not
open operations, write logs, commit or refresh indexes. Before any authorized
mutation, read [operation completion](operations.md); before quoting or
synthesizing, read [evidence](evidence.md).

Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs to the generated catalog. Search
diagnostics describe coverage, not relevance: a stale index can omit useful pages.
Read current passages and disclose weak or failed channels. Index freshness is
distinct from factual review dates.

## Choose the supported channel

| Operation | Channel and fallback |
|---|---|
| Read a Markdown page or source | CLI `read path=...`, or read its exact path under the known vault root. |
| Search | Prefer `search.mjs` and inspect its diagnostics. If a channel fails, use available results plus bounded filesystem `rg` over `wiki/` and `moc/`; include `raw/clippings/` only for evidence lookup. State missing channels. |
| Health, evidence routes, identity, relationships, drift coverage | Bundled filesystem helpers work without Obsidian. Do not gate them on `assertRunning`. Drift embeddings still require their backend. |
| Factual freshness report | `stale.mjs` may use CLI discovery or scoped filesystem fallback. Preserve missing-review and coverage diagnostics. |
| Ordinary Markdown creation/editing | Use exact-path filesystem edits even when the CLI is healthy, with the same operation, evidence, schema and validation contract. Read current content before editing; preserve unrelated changes. Never pass a whole note body through `content=`. |
| Small typed property or app actions | Use the guarded CLI entry point below; filesystem property edits remain available with schema validation. |
| Opening a note in the UI, executing an Obsidian/plugin command, app state, live Bases queries | Requires working Obsidian CLI. Report the specific unavailable action; continue independent file work. Do not pretend a filesystem approximation executed an app action. |

For CLI calls use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/obsidian.mjs" <command> ...`
or the bundled `scripts/lib/vault.mjs` API. These share an OS-managed lock across
agent processes, vaults and plugin copies for the same user. Do not launch native
`obsidian` directly or bypass a busy guard; other tools' raw calls are not protected.
The guard waits up to 10 seconds for a turn, then fails without sending a request.
Command execution has its own 10-second default timeout. Each request is limited
to a conservative 2,048-byte UTF-8 JSON envelope and rejects physical CR/LF/NUL.
This policy is not Obsidian's documented maximum. If rejected before sending,
use filesystem Markdown editing or narrow the read query; do not split a note
into many CLI writes or disable the guard. No fallback performs writes implicitly.
After an unavailable CLI or timeout, choose the supported fallback once; never
loop waiting for the app. **A timed-out mutation has an uncertain outcome.** Read
the exact target and check the intended effect before retrying or switching to
filesystem writes. An exit or timeout alone does not establish that nothing ran.
OS cleanup releases a lock after process death, but cannot prove a surviving CLI
child or an already-submitted Obsidian mutation finished. Inspect uncertain targets.

Validate resolved paths stay under the known root. Restrict searches to explicit
content directories; exclude `.recycle/`, dot folders, dependency trees and binary
originals. Do not recursively enumerate the entire user profile or scan a recycled
topic. Raw bodies remain immutable even during fallback. If target content changed
since it was read, reconcile it before writing; do not overwrite concurrent work.

## Shell portability

Examples elsewhere use `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs"` as command
notation. Replace the placeholder with the actual installed absolute path before
execution, and set the vault for the operation's scope. Do not execute literal
angle-bracket placeholders or assume a relative `scripts/` path means the plugin.

PowerShell (restore any prior environment value):

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki health failed' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

POSIX shell (one command's environment only):

```sh
WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault' node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/health.mjs'
```

On Windows, use PowerShell or the Node wrapper for Obsidian; Git Bash can select
the GUI executable instead of `Obsidian.com` and return misleading empty output.
These reporting examples are read-only: do not open an operation or rebuild the
index merely to answer a question.
